prompt:
Paint FOUR genuinely different chronological WALK animation poses of the same Qin He from the two owned reference images. Qin is the olive-clad staff woman in image1 and ONLY the bottom-right portrait in image2. The output is a 2×2 sprite sheet on a TRUE TRANSPARENT background, target1024×1024. Each cell is512×512, full-body single figure, head-to-boot height about390 pixels, centered with at least50 pixels empty padding on every cell edge. No text, grid, scenery, shadow or watermark.

ALL FOUR POSES show exactly the same RIGHT-FACING side profile, walking toward the right edge. Camera, face direction, torso, costume, figure scale and floor baseline stay identical. ANATOMY and leg silhouettes must differ strongly:

TOP LEFT = CONTACT A. The anatomical right leg (near leg) is extended far forward to screen-right, almost straight; right heel touching ground. Left leg extended far backward to screen-left, left toe on ground. The boots are FAR APART horizontally, about120 pixels. Both legs visible with open inverted-V gap. Bamboo staff right hand mostly vertical at right side.

TOP RIGHT = PASSING A. Weight on right leg vertically under pelvis, right boot FLAT on ground. Left leg bends90degrees AT KNEE, left knee advances toward screen-right and LEFT BOOT LIFTS clearly off ground, passing close beside the right supporting ankle. Boots are CLOSE together horizontally, within35 pixels. No split stance, no long stride here. Strong narrow silhouette distinct from top-left.

BOTTOM LEFT = CONTACT B. Swap the legs and visible overlap: anatomical LEFT leg (far leg) stretched far forward to screen-right with left heel down; anatomical RIGHT leg (near leg) stretched backward to screen-left with right toe down. Boots FAR APART again about120 pixels. Make near/right leg visibly behind now instead of repeating top-left. Slight natural arm counter-swing.

BOTTOM RIGHT = PASSING B. Weight on LEFT leg vertically under pelvis, left boot flat on ground. RIGHT leg near viewer flexes90degrees at knee and right boot LIFTS visibly beside left supporting ankle as right knee advances right. Boots CLOSE together within35 pixels. Knee and boot overlap opposite top-right, no split stance.

Preserve Qin's identity EXACTLY: young adult Chinese woman, gray-black hair pinned in bun with woodpin and teal ties, olive weathered layered short travel robe, ivory loose sleeves, rope belt, dark-gray trousers, brown wrapped boots, brown satchel/backpack and asymmetric belt bags, the long bamboo staff with wrappings and teal tassel. Same realistic painted watercolor/ink style as references; no new outfit. Carry staff in anatomical RIGHT hand throughout and keep its full length visible inside each cell. Left arm counter-swings; cloth moves subtly but legs and lifted boots remain readable. The four poses must be visibly WIDE, NARROW, WIDE WITH OTHER LEG, NARROW WITH OTHER LEG. Do not give four copies of a long split-stride pose.

Edit only the BOTTOM TWO FIGURES of this Qin He right-facing walk sheet. Keep the top two figures unchanged, and keep the same transparent canvas, face, hair, olive/ivory outfit, staff in her anatomical RIGHT hand, body scale and right-facing camera in all figures. Preserve the whole staff and boots without clipping.

The bottom two currently repeat the top two legs. They must show the OPPOSITE HALF of the walking cycle. This is the only change:
BOTTOM LEFT: Her near/right thigh must visibly sweep from the pelvis FORWARD toward SCREEN RIGHT and be drawn IN FRONT OF / OVERLAP the other thigh. Continue that near right shin diagonally down-right into the forward boot. Her far/left leg must go BACK toward SCREEN LEFT, partially occluded behind the near thigh and robe. Far boot rear at screen-left. Put a visible knee/fabric fold on the advancing near thigh. Keep the two feet separated in a wide stride. This must look like the OTHER leg is leading compared to top-left, not a repeat.
BOTTOM RIGHT: Her near/right leg must be the planted SUPPORT LEG, running almost vertically down from the pelvis into the grounded boot. Her far/left thigh comes FORWARD but passes BEHIND the near thigh; its knee is bent and its foot is lifted behind/beside the planted ankle, with only the lower boot peeking through at screen-right. Clearly a narrow passing position. Unlike top-right, the near thigh is straight, not the prominent raised rounded knee. Avoid both legs bent. Show a clear weight-bearing straight near leg.

Paint natural anatomy and original watercolor/ink texture. No mirroring the character, no new design or equipment, no changes to top row, no text, no shadows, no background.

Create FOUR distinct FRONT-FACING WALK poses of the same Qin He from the owned references: the staff woman in image1 and only the BOTTOM-RIGHT portrait in image2. Exactly2×2 full-body sprites on TRUE TRANSPARENT RGBA, target1024×1024. Same scale, camera, clothing and face. Each sprite has generous60pixel padding in its512cell. No text, grid, background or shadow.

She walks straight TOWARD THE VIEWER, looking directly forward, no side profile. Both boots stay separate on two tracks shoulder-width apart. Full bamboo staff in ANATOMICAL RIGHT hand means SCREEN LEFT for all4 poses; the staff NEVER changes hands. Show the whole staff.

TOP LEFT: LEFT-FOOT CONTACT. Her anatomical LEFT leg is ahead, so the SCREEN-RIGHT boot is straight and LOWEST near the floor; the screen-left right boot is behind, smaller and HIGHER. A visible18–30pixel vertical offset separates boot toes.
TOP RIGHT: PASSING. Weight on screen-right LEFT boot, left leg straight. Screen-left RIGHT knee bends and rises; right boot visibly lifts and passes beside the left shin, toes pointing downward and20–40pixels above ground. Legs remain visibly separate.
BOTTOM LEFT: RIGHT-FOOT CONTACT. SWAP THE LEGS. SCREEN-LEFT right boot is now straight and LOWEST near floor, screen-right left boot is behind and HIGHER. Both boots visible. This must clearly reverse the front-contact pose, not repeat it.
BOTTOM RIGHT: OPPOSITE PASSING. Weight on screen-left RIGHT boot. SCREEN-RIGHT left knee bends and rises; left boot visibly lifts beside right shin. Again reverse the top-right anatomy.

Preserve original face, gray-black pinned bun with teal ribbons, olive layered travel robe, cream sleeves, rope waist sash, dark-gray baggy pants, brown wrapped boots, asymmetric pouches and brown backpack. Calf/boot shapes must be visible below the hem. Adult realistic proportions, detailed muted Chinese watercolor and ink painting as refs. Staff held upright naturally at right side, right shoulder stable, left arm swings with walk. Natural calm walking, no battle/running/dance/extra limbs. Crown, pelvis and screen foot registration should stay stable; subtle torso bob2–4pixels only. Paint FOUR different anatomical phases, not four variations of the same front stance.

Correct ONLY the LEGS AND BOOTS of the two BOTTOM figures. Keep top row, faces, hair, torsos, olive/ivory clothing, belts, hands and staffs unchanged. True transparent background stays.

BOTTOM LEFT currently has the big forward boot on SCREEN LEFT, exactly like top-left. REVERSE its leg phase: draw the big straight forward boot on SCREEN RIGHT at ground level. Draw the screen-left boot BEHIND and higher, smaller, its heel raised. Move the corresponding knee/trouser folds to match. Do not mirror the entire figure: staff must remain SCREEN LEFT, held in same hand. Only reverse legs below hip.

BOTTOM RIGHT currently has SCREEN LEFT knee raised and screen-right boot supporting, same as top-right. REVERSE its leg phase: SCREEN RIGHT knee now lifted and bent with screen-right boot20–45pixels above the floor beside the other shin. SCREEN LEFT leg now straight and supporting, large screen-left boot planted at ground. Do not flip the torso, staff or face.

The resulting four frames must show: top-left screen-left boot leading; top-right screen-left knee lifted; bottom-left screen-RIGHT boot leading; bottom-right screen-RIGHT knee lifted. Both separate boot silhouettes visible. This is one4-phase walk cycle, so opposite halves must use opposite legs. Maintain original detailed painted watercolor/ink texture and adult realistic anatomy. No additions, background, grid, labels, extra limbs or cast shadow.

Make exactly ONE local accessory correction to this four-pose FRONT walking sprite sheet. In the BOTTOM LEFT figure, the brown rectangular tool pouch holding bamboo pieces is on the wrong side. Remove it from SCREEN LEFT waist and put the same single pouch at SCREEN RIGHT waist, matching the TOP LEFT figure. Do not move her hands or staff. Staff remains SCREEN LEFT, held by anatomical right hand.

Keep every other pixel/content as close as possible: all four leg and boot poses must stay EXACTLY as they are, including bottom-left large forward boot on SCREEN RIGHT and bottom-right raised SCREEN RIGHT knee. Preserve faces, bun, teal ribbons, robe, original painting style, body size and transparency. Do not flip torso or legs, do not duplicate or add pouches. Only reposition the bottom-left brown tool pouch. No background, text, border or shadow.

Create a 2×2 original walking-animation sheet of Qin He viewed DIRECTLY FROM BEHIND, all4 figures facing away and walking away. Reference1 is the owned character combat sheet; reference2 bottom-right portrait is Qin. Preserve her olive and ivory layered short travel robe, dark-gray trousers, wrapped brown boots, pinned dark-gray bun/woodpin, teal ribbons, brown back satchel and asymmetric left-waist pouch. Back of head and shoulders only, NO FACE. Adult proportions and same detailed muted watercolor/ink painting. Carry her entire bamboo staff in ANATOMICAL RIGHT hand: on SCREEN RIGHT in this back view, with tassel near top and lower tip near ground in every pose. Her free left arm counter-swings.

Transparent RGBA1024×1024, exactly4 full-body figures, one per quadrant, clear empty gutters/padding. No scenery, ground, cast shadow, labels or borders. Same body size, camera and foot ground for all four.

4 ANATOMICALLY DIFFERENT WALK phases. Both boots always visible separately, side-by-side tracks, not occluded by the robe. Feet are viewed from behind with soles visible when lifted.
TOP LEFT CONTACT: SCREEN-LEFT boot is the near grounded boot LOWEST in image; SCREEN-RIGHT boot extends ahead away from camera and is HIGHER. Two different ankle heights.
TOP RIGHT PASSING: SCREEN-LEFT leg straight supporting on floor. SCREEN-RIGHT knee flexes, RIGHT boot lifts with sole visible, clearly off ground beside the planted calf.
BOTTOM LEFT OPPOSITE CONTACT: REVERSE THE FEET, SCREEN-RIGHT boot is LOWEST planted, SCREEN-LEFT boot is HIGHER ahead away from camera. Keep torso/equipment/staff orientation unchanged.
BOTTOM RIGHT OPPOSITE PASSING: SCREEN-RIGHT leg straight and supporting on floor; SCREEN-LEFT knee flexes with left boot lifted off ground and sole visible beside right calf. Opposite top-right leg.
The bottom two must unmistakably reverse which boot is planted or lifted compared with top two. Do not repeat one gait half. Staff stays SCREEN RIGHT for all4, satchel and pouch stay on the same anatomical sides, do not mirror entire figures.

Make a precise small correction to this4-pose BACK-VIEW walk sheet of Qin. Preserve original faces-turned-away, pinned hair/ribbons, body scale, painting style, clothes, full staffs on SCREEN RIGHT, and true transparency.

1. In BOTTOM LEFT ONLY, change the lifted SCREEN-LEFT foot to an ordinary FORWARD CONTACT instead of a raised passing pose. Keep screen-right right leg straight with right boot at the low floor. Straighten the screen-left left knee; extend left foot forward away from camera so its boot is somewhat higher in image, toe contacting the ground. Show the BACK of that boot, not its full sole. Both knees should be nearly straight in this bottom-left contact. Bottom-right remains the raised-left-knee passing pose. Thus bottom-left and bottom-right must visibly differ.
2. Correct the brown rectangular bamboo-tool WAIST POUCH in ALL FOUR back views. There should be ONE left-waist pouch on SCREEN LEFT (her anatomical LEFT side) consistent with the original character. Remove the brown pouch on SCREEN RIGHT and show it hanging SCREEN LEFT instead. Keep central backpack unchanged, no extra pouch. Staff remains in SCREEN RIGHT hand. Do not mirror whole sprites or change boots in the other three frames.

Only these changes. No new equipment, text, border, ground or shadows.

Precision edit of two small areas only. Keep all four figures, transparent canvas, painted texture, faces turned away, staff on screen-right, and all other clothing/art unchanged.

BOTTOM-LEFT figure: REVERSE ONLY THE TWO LOWER LEGS. The SCREEN-RIGHT boot must be LOWEST, long and planted at the floor. The SCREEN-LEFT boot must end HIGHER by about45pixels, behind/ahead in depth with heel raised. Swap the current left-low/right-high relationship to RIGHT-LOW/LEFT-HIGH. Both legs nearly straight, contact pose, no visible full sole and no raised knee. Keep her torso and staff unflipped.

BOTTOM-RIGHT figure: Move its brown rectangular tool pouch from the SCREEN-RIGHT waist to SCREEN-LEFT waist, matching the other three figures. Remove the screen-right pouch. Do NOT change this figure's existing raised screen-left boot or grounded screen-right leg.

Only these corrections; no changes to top row, no new accessories/text/background, no mirroring of entire figures.

Create FOUR distinct LEFT-FACING walking-animation poses of Qin He from the owned refs. She is the olive-clad staff woman in image1 and bottom-right portrait in image2. Exact2×2 transparent RGBA sprite sheet, one full-body figure per quadrant, no text/background/shadow/grid. Keep full character and whole bamboo staff within generous60pixel padding. Same adult proportions, face, gray-black pinned bun with teal ribbons, olive layered robe and ivory sleeves, rope sash, gray baggy trousers, brown wrapped boots, backpack and left-waist pouch. Original muted watercolor/ink style. Her face and torso face LEFT in all4, she walks screen-left.

This is her LEFT anatomical side seen by camera. Staff must be held in FAR / anatomical RIGHT HAND, behind her torso, not in the visible near left hand. Show staff mostly vertical on far side at screen-left, partially occluded by body; visible left arm is FREE and swings. Do not mirror a right-facing drawing.

TOP LEFT WIDE CONTACT: Near anatomical LEFT leg stretches forward to SCREEN LEFT with heel planted; FAR right leg extends BACK toward screen-right with toe planted. Big open upside-down-V between legs; feet about120pixels apart. Near left thigh visibly passes IN FRONT OF far thigh.
TOP RIGHT NARROW PASSING: Near LEFT leg supports nearly vertically on ground; FAR right knee bends90degrees, far boot LIFTS off ground and passes BEHIND near ankle, peeking beside it. Feet nearly together horizontally.
BOTTOM LEFT OPPOSITE WIDE CONTACT: FAR RIGHT leg now leads toward SCREEN LEFT, near LEFT leg trails to SCREEN RIGHT. Near thigh drawn in front but sweeps BACKWARD this time. Two boots far apart again; leg overlap reversed compared with top-left.
BOTTOM RIGHT OPPOSITE NARROW PASSING: FAR RIGHT leg now supports vertically; NEAR LEFT knee is visibly raised toward screen-left, its boot lifted in FRONT OF the far supporting shin. Different bent-knee silhouette from top-right.

The four silhouettes must go wide/narrow/wide/narrow, and the bottom pair must clearly use the opposite leg. Keep staff in far right hand and near left hand free throughout, equipment on correct anatomical sides, face and body not mirrored between cells. Minimal natural cloth motion; clearly readable two-leg human walking, not running or four repeated stances.
